The stage is smaller – the subs will go in a line under the front edge. I marked the positions with tape. The monitor desk is still noisy on the aux sends – I mentioned it to the production manager last week – he said he will look into it. No word yet.

**3 Oct 2025, Fri** – Soundcheck for the corporate event at 14:00. The client is a bank – they have a keynote and a panel. The setup:
- 4 handheld mics – 2 for the panel, 1 for the host, 1 spare
- 2 lavs for the speakers who move around
- Laptop feed for the slides – chk'd the DI – fine
- The panel table has 3 chairs – the mics are on stands – no table stands available – I used short booms – OK

The soundcheck went well – the room is a bit live – the ceiling is hard – I added a bit of reverb to the mics – the client liked it. The subs are fine – the repositioning worked – no boominess.

**4 Oct 2025, Sat** – Corporate event day. I arrived at 07:30 – the client wanted a full rehearsal at 08:30. The rehearsal went fine – no issues. The keynote speaker used a lav – it was a bit quiet – I turned up the gain – better. The panel went well – no feedback. The event ended at 17:00 – I struck the mics and the DI – the PA stays for the next event.

**5 Oct 2025, Sun** – Day off – but I came in to do a bit of maintenance. The monitor desk is still noisy – I opened it up – the caps on the aux sends are old – that is the cause. I will order new caps – but the desk is not urgent – it works – just noisy. I will mention it again to the production manager.

**6 Oct 2025, Mon** – The next event is a product launch on the main stage – this Thursday. The client wants a specific look – a white stage – the PA needs to be flown – the subs will be hidden behind a false wall. I did a rough plan – the subs will be in a row – the false wall will be built tomorrow. I will need to chk the alignment – the wall may block some of the highs.

**7 Oct 2025, Tue** – The false wall is up – the subs are behind it. I did a quick test – the sound is a bit muffled – the wall is absorbing some of the high end – but the subs are fine – the low end is unaffected. I will add a bit of EQ to the tops – a small shelf at 3kHz – should be OK. The client wants a walkthrough tomorrow.

**8 Oct 2025, Wed** – Walkthrough with the client – they liked the sound – no complaints. They want the music to be louder during the demo – I turned up the playback – the limiter is on – it is fine. The mics are set – 2 handheld, 1 lav for the presenter. The lav is a bit quiet – I will swap it for a different one – the one I have is old.

**9 Oct 2025, Thu** – Product launch day. Soundcheck at 09:00 – went long – until 10:30. The client kept changing the levels – but that is normal. Issues:
- The lav was still quiet – I swapped it – the new one is better
- The playback had a small click at the start – chk'd the file – it was in the source – not our gear – OK
- The subs were a bit boomy – the false wall is reflecting the low end – I cut 60Hz a bit – better

The event went well – no major issues. The client was happy.

**10 Oct 2025, Fri** – Day off. I came in to do a bit of work – the monitor desk caps arrived – I replaced them – took about 2 hours. The desk is much quieter now – no more noise on the aux sends. I will note that in the log – the desk is fixed.
**11 Nov 2025, Tue** – Festival prep week starts today. The big one – 3 days, 4 stages. I am on the main stage (Stage A) and also covering the acoustic tent when needed. Did the load-in this morning – the truck was late by 45 min, so we lost some time. The crew is good – they know the drill. We got the PA stacks in place by 14:00. The subs are the same set from the product launch – they are fine, just a bit of a rumble at idle – I noted that before. I will chk the power distro tomorrow – the cable run is long and I want to see the voltage drop.

**12 Nov 2025, Wed** – Load-in day 2. Got the monitor wedges out – 8 total for the main stage. 4 are the newer ones, 4 are the older ones – the older ones have a bit of a rattle at high volume – not urgent, but I will keep them on the side for the smaller acts. The acoustic tent has its own small PA – 2 tops on sticks – easy. The tent is right next to the food stalls – the generator is loud – the stage manager said they will move the generator – I am not holding my breath. Chk'd the power distro – voltage is fine, 230V – the long cable run is OK. The line check took a bit longer than expected because one of the stage snakes had a bad channel – chn 12 – I swapped it with a spare – the spare is a bit short – I will tape it down tomorrow.

**13 Nov 2025, Thu** – Final setup day. Did the full system check this morning – walked the stage with the production manager. The PA is flown – the subs are on the ground in front – that is the standard config for this stage. The false wall from the product launch is not here – good – this is an open-air stage. The wind is a concern – it is gusty – the flown PA should be OK, but I will chk the rigging points tomorrow morning. The monitor mixes are set – I did a quick test with a vocal mic – the levels are good. The acoustic tent is set – the small PA is fine – the generator is still there – the stage manager said they will move it – I will believe it when I see it. The food stalls are on the other side – the smell is fine – the noise is not. I will bring earplugs for the tent.

**14 Nov 2025, Fri – Day 1** – Festival day 1. Soundcheck at 08:00 – the first act is a local indie band – they want a lot of reverb on the vocals – I gave them a bit – they asked for more – I gave them more – they were happy. The second act is a DJ – they have their own controller – I just need to give them a stereo feed – easy. The third act is a singer-songwriter – acoustic guitar and vocal – she is in the tent – the generator is still there – I asked the stage manager again – he said they will move it during the lunch break – we will see.

Issues today:
- The monitor wedges – the older ones are rattling – I swapped one out during the band's set – the spare is fine.
- The stage snake – chn 12 is still not reliable – I used a different channel – chn 24 – I will note that in the patch sheet.
- The acoustic tent – the vocal mic is feeding back a bit – the tent is small and the PA is close – I cut a bit of 1kHz – better.

The band's set went well – no major issues. The DJ was fine – the stereo feed was clean. The singer-songwriter was good – the tent is small but the sound is OK – the generator is still there – I will mention it again.

**14 Nov 2025, Fri – Evening** – The main stage is done for today – the last act finished at 22:30 – the crowd was good – no issues. I did a quick walkthrough of the stage – the gear is all there – no damage. The monitor wedges are back in the case – the older ones are marked – I will fix them after the festival. The acoustic tent is closed – the small PA is covered – the generator is still there – the stage manager said they will move it tomorrow – I will believe it when I see it.
**15 Nov 2025, Sat – Wrap-up / Teardown Day 3**

Woke up early – 06:30 – went straight to the stage. The overnight crew had already started on the main stage – the truss is down and the subs are on the dolly. Good pace. I did a quick walkthrough to spot any damage before the gear gets loaded.

Main stage gear condition after the festival:
- FOH desk – clean, no faders broken. The scribble strips are faded but that was already known.
- Stage snake – chn 12 is still unreliable. I marked the channel with red tape and put a note on the patch sheet. Will test the cable after we are back at the shop.
- Monitor wedges – the older ones are rattling. I marked them "SVC" – two of them. The spares are fine.
- Vocal mics – all accounted for. Need a clean and a new windscreen on the one that got dropped on Day 2.
- Drum mics – all present. The kick mic clip is cracked – will replace.
- DI boxes – 6 returned, 2 still in the acoustic tent? I will chk when I get there.

The generator in the acoustic tent is still there. The stage manager said they will move it this morning – I will believe it when I see it. I walked past the tent at 07:15 – it was still running. The sound of it was fine but the smell is not. I will ask again.

**Teardown notes – acoustic tent**

The small PA came down easy. The vocal mic was feeding back a bit on the last day – I cut 1kHz again and it was better. The tent is small and the PA is close – that is the main issue. For next year, we should consider a different placement or a smaller PA in the tent. I will note that in the debrief.

The tent itself is in OK shape – the side panels are a bit dusty but no rips. The generator – still there. I will chk again after the main stage is loaded.

**Packing list – main stage**

Cables – all coiled and bagged. I found one XLR with a broken latch – will replace. The power distro is back on the pallet – the electrician signed it off. The stage deck is being swept – no loose screws found.

I did a final count of the mics – 24 total – all match the inventory sheet. The clip on the kick mic is cracked – I noted it. The monitor wedges are in the case – the two marked "SVC" are at the top so they get fixed first.

**Returns and loans**

- The DJ's controller – returned to the artist's manager at 09:00. They confirmed receipt – no issues.
- The extra DI boxes – 2 were on loan from the rental house – they are back in the truck. I will call them on Monday to confirm the return.
- The acoustic tent PA – it is our own gear – no return needed.

I still have the key to the storage locker – will return it to the office on Monday.

**Lessons learned – quick notes for the debrief**

- The generator in the acoustic tent – it was a problem all three days. We should have a plan for the generator placement before the festival starts. The stage manager said they will move it – but they did not. We need a written schedule for the generator move.
- The monitor wedges – the older ones are rattling. We should replace them or fix them before the next event. The spares are fine but we only have two.
- The stage snake – chn 12 is unreliable. We should test the whole snake before the next festival and replace the bad channel or the cable.
- The vocal mic in the tent – feeding back is a recurring issue. We should test the PA placement before the act arrives. The 1kHz cut helps but it is not a full fix.

**Final checks – 15 Nov 2025, Sat**

- 10:30 – Main stage is clear. All gear is on the truck. I did a final walkthrough – no cables left, no stands left. The stage deck is clean.
- 10:45 – Acoustic tent – the small PA is packed. The generator is still there. The stage manager said they will move it after lunch – I will believe it when I see it. I left a note on the generator with my number.
- 11:00 – Truck is loaded. I will do a final inventory count when we get back to the shop.

documents.content:

**20 Sept 2025, Sat** – Festival main stage. Wind picked up in the afternoon, more than forecast. Stage left canopy flap was catching – tied down with extra rope. The PA wings were rocking a bit. Chk'd the ratchet straps on the delay tower – one was loose – tightened. No damage.

**24 Sept 2025, Wed** – Soundcheck for the second stage is scheduled for Sat 09:00. I will be there with the stage crew. The guest engineer for that stage is a guy named Raj – he is from the local hire company. I have not worked with him before – will see how he is.

The subs are fine. The monitor desk is a bit noisy on the aux sends – chk'd the grounding – it is OK, just old. Will mention to the production manager.

**26 Sept 2025, Fri** – Final prep for the second stage. The stage is set up – the canopy is up – the PA is flown. The drum kit is on the riser. The mics are patched. I did a quick line check with the stage crew – all good. The festival continues – tomorrow is the first day with both stages running. - The vocal mics are feeding back a bit – the stage is small and the wedges are close – I added a bit of a notch at 2.5kHz – better

- The keyboard DI had a low hum – chk'd the ground – it was the DI itself – swapped it – clean now

documents.title: Sound Engineering Notebook – Marcus Lee
documents.content:
**1 Oct 2025, Wed** – Back after the maintenance week. Full cable sweep done – found 3 bad XLRs and 1 bad speakon. Pulled them from stock. The drum kit heads arrived – installed them on the kit for the second stage. Took about an hour. The kit sounds much better – the old heads were dead.

**2 Oct 2025, Thu** – The festival is over but there is a corporate event on the main stage next week. I started the changeover – the flown PA stays, but the subs need to be repositioned. The stage is smaller – the subs will go in a line under the front edge. I marked the positions with tape. The monitor desk is still noisy on the aux sends – I mentioned it to the production manager last week – he said he will look into it. No word yet.

**3 Oct 2025, Fri** – Soundcheck for the corporate event at 14:00. The client is a bank – they have a keynote and a panel. The setup:
- 4 handheld mics – 2 for the panel, 1 for the host, 1 spare
- 2 lavs for the speakers who move around
- Laptop feed for the slides – chk'd the DI – fine
- The panel table has 3 chairs – the mics are on stands – no table stands available – I used short booms – OK

The soundcheck went well – the room is a bit live – the ceiling is hard – I added a bit of reverb to the mics – the client liked it. The subs are fine – the repositioning worked – no boominess.

**4 Oct 2025, Sat** – Corporate event day. I arrived at 07:30 – the client wanted a full rehearsal at 08:30. The rehearsal went fine – no issues. The keynote speaker used a lav – it was a bit quiet – I turned up the gain – better. The panel went well – no feedback. The event ended at 17:00 – I struck the mics and the DI – the PA stays for the next event.

**5 Oct 2025, Sun** – Day off – but I came in to do a bit of maintenance. The monitor desk is still noisy – I opened it up – the caps on the aux sends are old – that is the cause. I will order new caps – but the desk is not urgent – it works – just noisy. I will mention it again to the production manager.

**6 Oct 2025, Mon** – The next event is a product launch on the main stage – this Thursday. The client wants a specific look – a white stage – the PA needs to be flown – the subs will be hidden behind a false wall. I did a rough plan – the subs will be in a row – the false wall will be built tomorrow. I will need to chk the alignment – the wall may block some of the highs.

**7 Oct 2025, Tue** – The false wall is up – the subs are behind it. I did a quick test – the sound is a bit muffled – the wall is absorbing some of the high end – but the subs are fine – the low end is unaffected. I will add a bit of EQ to the tops – a small shelf at 3kHz – should be OK. The client wants a walkthrough tomorrow.

**8 Oct 2025, Wed** – Walkthrough with the client – they liked the sound – no complaints. They want the music to be louder during the demo – I turned up the playback – the limiter is on – it is fine. The mics are set – 2 handheld, 1 lav for the presenter. The lav is a bit quiet – I will swap it for a different one – the one I have is old.

**9 Oct 2025, Thu** – Product launch day. Soundcheck at 09:00 – went long – until 10:30. The client kept changing the levels – but that is normal. Issues:
- The lav was still quiet – I swapped it – the new one is better
- The playback had a small click at the start – chk'd the file – it was in the source – not our gear – OK
- The subs were a bit boomy – the false wall is reflecting the low end – I cut 60Hz a bit – better

The event went well – no major issues. The client was happy.

**10 Oct 2025, Fri** – Day off. I came in to do a bit of work – the monitor desk caps arrived – I replaced them – took about 2 hours. The desk is much quieter now – no more noise on the aux sends. I will note that in the log – the desk is fixed.

documents.title: Sound Engineering Notebook – Marcus Lee
documents.content:
**11 Nov 2025, Tue** – Festival prep week starts today. The big one – 3 days, 4 stages. I am on the main stage (Stage A) and also covering the acoustic tent when needed. Did the load-in this morning – the truck was late by 45 min, so we lost some time. The crew is good – they know the drill. We got the PA stacks in place by 14:00. The subs are the same set from the product launch – they are fine, just a bit of a rumble at idle – I noted that before. I will chk the power distro tomorrow – the cable run is long and I want to see the voltage drop.

**12 Nov 2025, Wed** – Load-in day 2. Got the monitor wedges out – 8 total for the main stage. 4 are the newer ones, 4 are the older ones – the older ones have a bit of a rattle at high volume – not urgent, but I will keep them on the side for the smaller acts. The acoustic tent has its own small PA – 2 tops on sticks – easy. The tent is right next to the food stalls – the generator is loud – the stage manager said they will move the generator – I am not holding my breath. Chk'd the power distro – voltage is fine, 230V – the long cable run is OK. The line check took a bit longer than expected because one of the stage snakes had a bad channel – chn 12 – I swapped it with a spare – the spare is a bit short – I will tape it down tomorrow.

**13 Nov 2025, Thu** – Final setup day. Did the full system check this morning – walked the stage with the production manager. The PA is flown – the subs are on the ground in front – that is the standard config for this stage. The false wall from the product launch is not here – good – this is an open-air stage. The wind is a concern – it is gusty – the flown PA should be OK, but I will chk the rigging points tomorrow morning. The monitor mixes are set – I did a quick test with a vocal mic – the levels are good. The acoustic tent is set – the small PA is fine – the generator is still there – the stage manager said they will move it – I will believe it when I see it. The food stalls are on the other side – the smell is fine – the noise is not. I will bring earplugs for the tent.

**14 Nov 2025, Fri – Day 1** – Festival day 1. Soundcheck at 08:00 – the first act is a local indie band – they want a lot of reverb on the vocals – I gave them a bit – they asked for more – I gave them more – they were happy. The second act is a DJ – they have their own controller – I just need to give them a stereo feed – easy. The third act is a singer-songwriter – acoustic guitar and vocal – she is in the tent – the generator is still there – I asked the stage manager again – he said they will move it during the lunch break – we will see.

Issues today:
- The monitor wedges – the older ones are rattling – I swapped one out during the band's set – the spare is fine.
- The stage snake – chn 12 is still not reliable – I used a different channel – chn 24 – I will note that in the patch sheet.
- The acoustic tent – the vocal mic is feeding back a bit – the tent is small and the PA is close – I cut a bit of 1kHz – better.

The band's set went well – no major issues. The DJ was fine – the stereo feed was clean. The singer-songwriter was good – the tent is small but the sound is OK – the generator is still there – I will mention it again.

**14 Nov 2025, Fri – Evening** – The main stage is done for today – the last act finished at 22:30 – the crowd was good – no issues. I did a quick walkthrough of the stage – the gear is all there – no damage. The monitor wedges are back in the case – the older ones are marked – I will fix them after the festival. The acoustic tent is closed – the small PA is covered – the generator is still there – the stage manager said they will move it tomorrow – I will believe it when I see it.

documents.title: Sound Engineering Notebook – Marcus Lee
documents.content:
**15 Nov 2025, Sat – Wrap-up / Teardown Day 3**

Woke up early – 06:30 – went straight to the stage. The overnight crew had already started on the main stage – the truss is down and the subs are on the dolly. Good pace. I did a quick walkthrough to spot any damage before the gear gets loaded.

Main stage gear condition after the festival:
- FOH desk – clean, no faders broken. The scribble strips are faded but that was already known.
- Stage snake – chn 12 is still unreliable. I marked the channel with red tape and put a note on the patch sheet. Will test the cable after we are back at the shop.
- Monitor wedges – the older ones are rattling. I marked them "SVC" – two of them. The spares are fine.
- Vocal mics – all accounted for. Need a clean and a new windscreen on the one that got dropped on Day 2.
- Drum mics – all present. The kick mic clip is cracked – will replace.
- DI boxes – 6 returned, 2 still in the acoustic tent? I will chk when I get there.

The generator in the acoustic tent is still there. The stage manager said they will move it this morning – I will believe it when I see it. I walked past the tent at 07:15 – it was still running. The sound of it was fine but the smell is not. I will ask again.

**Teardown notes – acoustic tent**

The small PA came down easy. The vocal mic was feeding back a bit on the last day – I cut 1kHz again and it was better. The tent is small and the PA is close – that is the main issue. For next year, we should consider a different placement or a smaller PA in the tent. I will note that in the debrief.

The tent itself is in OK shape – the side panels are a bit dusty but no rips. The generator – still there. I will chk again after the main stage is loaded.

**Packing list – main stage**

Cables – all coiled and bagged. I found one XLR with a broken latch – will replace. The power distro is back on the pallet – the electrician signed it off. The stage deck is being swept – no loose screws found.

I did a final count of the mics – 24 total – all match the inventory sheet. The clip on the kick mic is cracked – I noted it. The monitor wedges are in the case – the two marked "SVC" are at the top so they get fixed first.

**Returns and loans**

- The DJ's controller – returned to the artist's manager at 09:00. They confirmed receipt – no issues.
- The extra DI boxes – 2 were on loan from the rental house – they are back in the truck. I will call them on Monday to confirm the return.
- The acoustic tent PA – it is our own gear – no return needed.

I still have the key to the storage locker – will return it to the office on Monday.

**Lessons learned – quick notes for the debrief**

- The generator in the acoustic tent – it was a problem all three days. We should have a plan for the generator placement before the festival starts. The stage manager said they will move it – but they did not. We need a written schedule for the generator move.
- The monitor wedges – the older ones are rattling. We should replace them or fix them before the next event. The spares are fine but we only have two.
- The stage snake – chn 12 is unreliable. We should test the whole snake before the next festival and replace the bad channel or the cable.
- The vocal mic in the tent – feeding back is a recurring issue. We should test the PA placement before the act arrives. The 1kHz cut helps but it is not a full fix.

**Final checks – 15 Nov 2025, Sat**

- 10:30 – Main stage is clear. All gear is on the truck. I did a final walkthrough – no cables left, no stands left. The stage deck is clean.
- 10:45 – Acoustic tent – the small PA is packed. The generator is still there. The stage manager said they will move it after lunch – I will believe it when I see it. I left a note on the generator with my number.
- 11:00 – Truck is loaded. I will do a final inventory count when we get back to the shop.

This summary covers the final week of the post-festival rental period for the Marina Bay event. All equipment was returned to the warehouse by 15 Nov 2025. The primary focus this week was on the condition inspection of returned units, the completion of the ENT05 firmware update, and the preparation of the maintenance schedule for the off-season.

The warehouse was quiet for most of the week, with only the returning units and the team conducting inspections. No show support was required. The next scheduled deployment is for the corporate year-end event in early December.

**2. Equipment Condition Reports – Post-Return Inspection**

All units were inspected upon return. The inspection was conducted by the warehouse team using the standard visual and functional checklist. The following table details the condition of each unit.
